does_not_establish: production capacity without a revision-bound measurement artifact
runtime performance from configured thresholds alone
database scalability from query-plan shape alone

budget.measurement: sum of unique modulepreload and stylesheet assets referenced by prerendered route HTML, gzip level 9

limitations: The thresholds are inherited from prior policy files and are not blocking until a revision-bound calibration artifact exists.
Synthetic browser samples do not establish production field performance.
The canonical browser proof uses deterministic API and basemap fixtures; real backend capacity belongs to api_runtime evidence.

The p95/p99 latency and failure-rate thresholds are blocking only for an evidence artifact whose measured API build_info commit matches the recorded git revision, whose domain-scale fixture manifest validates against the canonical measurements.database_scale config/profile, and whose live binding proves the isolated target database/search state matches that fixture; passing them does not establish production capacity.

The T048 mixed-health-and-read load is a post-start measurement: after three consecutive readiness HTTP 200 responses, a /health/ready HTTP 503 during the measured load counts toward http_request_failed_rate; earlier 503-tolerant run artifacts are not retrospectively reclassified.

The isolated T048 CI bulk fixture creates setup-only outbox entries through production database triggers. Only after validating fixture counts and rejecting unexpected, processed or quarantined outbox state, the disposable CI PostgreSQL database resets those setup-only events before API warm-up. T048 measures the steady-state read workload and does not establish bulk event ingestion throughput or durability.
Health-endpoint smoke checks alone do not establish API capacity.

scripts/performance/api_runtime_evidence.py check produces a machine-readable evidence artifact bound to the measured API build_info commit, the exact git HEAD, the validated domain-scale fixture manifest, the live database/search binding, the explicit search query, digest-pinned API/PostgreSQL/k6 image identities and this scenario contract; it reuses the existing search_request_duration_seconds, search_repository_duration_seconds and http_requests_total Prometheus telemetry rather than a new observability path, and its query-count evidence is a deterministic cross-check between two independently instrumented counters, not a sampled profiler.

search_repository_duration_seconds measures the API repository span for active-generation lookup plus authorized candidate retrieval and decoding; embedding-provider time is recorded separately by search_provider_duration_seconds, so this metric is not PostgreSQL-server-only execution time.

The live binding content-hashes all isolated domain_nodes against the deterministic fixture, binds the active search generation and projections to fixture nodes, and reads the search candidate safety limit from product source in the same git revision; this attests the experiment state only, not steady-state production capacity or production data distribution.

scripts/performance/api_runtime_evidence.py regression-fixture generates a self-consistent but threshold-violating fixture so the gate's fail-closed behaviour can be demonstrated and tested on demand.
Database latency and query-count evidence describe the search read path only; they do not establish plan-shape at scale, which remains the responsibility of measurements.database_scale.
Plan-shape checks do not establish end-to-end latency or concurrent throughput.
No blocking resource thresholds exist until reproducible measurements cover projection refresh and steady-state traffic.

Runner: scripts/performance/container_resource_sampler.py samples peak Docker CPU percent and cgroup memory bytes for the already-running API replica container over the same bounded window as the api_runtime k6 workload. These are peak_cpu_percent and peak_memory_bytes; they are not mislabeled as CPU-seconds or process max RSS.

Runner: scripts/performance/postgres_connection_sampler.py samples PostgreSQL's built-in pg_stat_activity connection count over the same bounded load window and records the maximum plus the underlying samples; no extension such as pg_stat_statements is required.

k6, the live database/search binding, the API resource receipt and the PostgreSQL connection receipt carry one explicit run_id. The API-resource and PostgreSQL sampler receipt intervals must cover the complete k6 load interval; api_runtime_evidence.py fails closed if run identities, measured container names or temporal coverage disagree, preventing stale or non-overlapping sampler output from being attached to a different load run.

These samples are attached to the api_runtime evidence artifact produced by scripts/performance/api_runtime_evidence.py check; they remain calibration_required until repeated across hardware baselines.
